_comment: Hashes of the upstream artefacts every bridge document cites. Truncated to 16 hex, which is what the schema's pattern allows. A mismatch is rule R6 and it means an import is stale, not that the file is wrong. WHAT IS HASHED: the bytes of one file. A ref naming a DIRECTORY has no content of its own -- `bd:runs/trap-2d-5um__a5ef4f45d589` is registered at its metrics.json, which is what its three citations already say in their `field`, and which is recorded in `_subject_of` rather than left as a convention somebody has to know. Regenerate with tools/rehash.sh, which PRINTS the lines to add and writes nothing: the round number is a human's to name, and refreshing an unsuffixed key invalidates every citation below it.
_am_note: A sender's own plan changes between rounds -- that is the round working -- and this file holds one value per key. The unsuffixed plan key is the r1-era file (rev 9f971a8) that r1 and r2 both cite and must keep verifying; '@r<N>' is a second key for the revision a later round was distilled from (rev 35575cb). One key per round, added by the owning side, nothing overwritten. This is not a substitute for the `rev` field the README now requires on a ref: `rev` says which revision a ref means, the suffixed key is what lets R6 check two of them. Unsuffixed keys are at rev 9f971a8; '@r3' is 35575cb, '@r4' and '@r5' are aeea29d, all on branch worktree-work-2026-09-16 of the AM repo. The r2 import has two keys because r4 corrected it: the body is unedited and only `corrected_by` was added, so the r1-era hash still verifies for anything citing it from before. ⚠ '@r9' was registered BEFORE r9 was written, at the revision that integrated r8, and the plan then moved again -- so it named a revision r9 does not cite, and a reader would have been pointed at a P7 that still said 'blocked on a data transfer'. Corrected in place rather than given a second key, because nothing cited it: grepped first. Register a round's key when that round is written, not in advance; a suffixed key is a record of what a document cites, and there is nothing to record before the document exists.
_bd_note: bd: keys are added by the BD session. verify/ entries are at rev 07d1048 on branch microscope-link-survey, not on BD's main; every ref carries `rev`. The r2 key is UNSUFFIXED at the revision r4 and AM's r4 import cite, and '@r8' is the revision after 4652273 added gaps[].kind. Refreshing the unsuffixed key instead was tried and CASCADED: r4 then had to be refreshed, which broke r5 and r7, which cite r4. A sealed document's citation must not move because a later commit added metadata upstream -- that is what the suffixed-key convention is for. r8 has two registered revisions: the unsuffixed key is the one AM's r8 import cites, and '@rev-corrected' is after 813fcf2 fixed a false rev on bd:verify/verify_ladder_tolerance.py. The content did not change -- only a revision string that resolved to nothing. Registered rather than refreshed, because refreshing a cited key is what caused the earlier cascade.
_subject_of_note: A key whose value is deliberately the hash of a DIFFERENT artefact, and the path that is actually read when `--resolve` opens it. Two entries. (1) r1's ask was distilled from AM's plan and AM held no separate file, so per r2's note this key carries the plan's hash and r7 cites it at the plan's rev. That fact lived in two prose notes, and the proposals file predicted the first regeneration would read it as a false 'moved upstream' -- it was right, `--resolve` was that regeneration. (2) A run directory has no bytes of its own; this one is registered at its metrics.json, which is what its three citations already say in `field` and what the registered value has always been (measured at the cited rev and at HEAD). Redirected rows print on every run even when they pass: a quiet exception is how (1) got forgotten.
